items.title: MISCOMPILE: a MODULE's platform-fenced twins are selected under the analyzer's DEFAULT platform, not the build's — a `target = "browser"` package whose module declares `[platform("browser")]` and `[platform("@process")]` twins ships the `@process` twin in its browser bundle (`return "process"`); the same twins in the ENTRY select correctly
items.discussion: editor-48 (Order 48), met building E254; sweeps/order48/editor-48/finds/module_twin_platform/; `analyze_inner` in analyzer.rs (incr-48's driver this order); F27 R3
items.body: Repro: `vilan build` in the find's package (browser target, entry `client.vl` calls `place()` from `src/place.vl`, which declares the two twins) emits `return "process";`; swap the twins' order and it still emits the process twin; move the twins into the entry and it emits `"browser"`. Two-entry packages (browser client + node server reaching one module) emit the process twin into BOTH bundles. ROOT CAUSE: `analyze_inner` walks the loaded modules — and calls `select_platform_twins` for each (analyzer.rs ~74938, `select_twins(items, text, self.platform)`) — before `analyzer.platform = platform` is assigned (~75715), so every module's twins are read against `Analyzer::new()`'s default platform (a process host). The entry's twins are selected after the assignment, which is why they are right. Verified: one line, `analyzer.platform = platform;` right after `Analyzer::new()` in `analyze_inner`, makes the browser bundle emit the browser twin and the server bundle the process twin (and makes editor-48's E254 pins pass). Not fixed here: `analyze_inner` is the pass driver incr-48 owns this order. Also check `analyze_over_world`/the hot-set world path for the same ordering. Pins owed: a module's twins on both legs through `native_differential`-style build of each entry, and the LSP view of a twin module (E254's held patch carries `e254_a_twin_file_is_served_from_the_world_that_admits_each_twin`). E254 is blocked on this.

items.title: a generic BOUND naming an unimported trait gets no import steer — `fun keep<T: Storable>(..)` is refused bare "cannot find type 'Storable'", where the same miss in an annotation or a path says "; import it first (`import std::reactive::store::Storable;`)"
items.discussion: editor-48 (Order 48), met pinning B572; sweeps/order48/editor-48/finds/bound_trait_steer/main.vl; the B4 import steer (`import_steer`)
items.body: `vilan check main.vl` on the find: the bound `T: Storable` is refused "cannot find type 'Storable'" with no steer, and the `Store::new(1)` below it gets "cannot find type 'Store'; import it first (`import std::reactive::store::Store;`)". The bound's miss is raised outside the type-position site that calls `import_steer` (analyzer.rs ~60401, `format!("cannot find type '{}'{}", name, steer)`), so it never asks. Fix: route the bound's miss through `import_steer` (and the add-import quick fix follows, since it keys on `cannot find`). Sizing XS; analyzer.rs (not editor-48's this order).

items.title: a file OPENED into a world another document already holds is served at once (M104's `serve_from_held_world`) but its FURTHER worlds are never analyzed — a module both a browser and a node entry reach shows only the browser leg's verdict until the next edit, where opened the other way round the open's sweep analyzes the node world
items.discussion: editor-48 (Order 48), met building E254 (the probe's kept-world map stayed empty); sweeps/order48/editor-48/finds/held_world_further/; `did_open` in vilan-lsp main.rs (LSP scheduling, incr-48's this order)
items.body: `did_open`: when `serve_from_held_world` serves the opened file it refreshes and RETURNS, skipping the branch below it that runs `reanalyze_dependents` when a landed document has `further_worlds` — the branch that analyzes a further world that should exist and does not (M104's own comment). So with `client.vl` open and settled, opening `shared.vl` (reached by the client and the server entries) leaves the server world unanalyzed: no node-leg diagnostics on the file (E113) and, with E254's held patch, no twin legs. Opening `shared.vl` first, then `client.vl`, analyzes it. Fix: after a held-world serve, schedule the sweep for the served document's further worlds that no kept world or open entry holds. Observed in an LSP test (`server.worlds` empty, the document's `further_worlds()` = the server entry); not built — LSP scheduling is incr-48's this order.
